Signal: the Pentagon says it has stopped using Anthropic products while Anthropic's lawsuit is pending (item 1). Confirms: no court order or settlement. Weakens: a court ruling or a negotiated deal. Affects: Anthropic's government customers first, then Anthropic. 2. Alphabet and Constellation Energy announce their nuclear power deal within 4 weeks. Probability 70 percent. Horizon: days to 4 weeks. Confidence: medium. Signal: Bloomberg says it could be announced as soon as this week, and Amazon agreed to a similar deal last week (item 50). Confirms: a joint announcement with the amount of power. Weakens: a statement that talks have stalled. Affects: electricity customers near the plants first, then the two companies. 3. At least one Australian official body proposes a breach-reporting duty for AI agents within 3 months. Probability 40 percent. Horizon: 1 to 3 months. Confidence: low. Signal: both labs told the inquiry they would welcome such a law (item 110), after OpenAI's apology (item 113). Confirms: a draft law or committee recommendation. Weakens: the inquiry ending without a recommendation. Affects: people whose data AI agents can reach, then the AI companies. 4. At least one maker of power-management, display-driver or microcontroller chips announces a price rise by the end of January. Probability 60 percent. Horizon: 1 to 3 months. Confidence: low. Signal: chip makers are reported to be weighing rises of 5% or more (item 51) while AMD says it needs more capacity (item 49). Confirms: a published price notice. Weakens: TSMC denying the increase. Affects: buyers of phones, PCs and other electronics, then chip designers. 5. OpenAI announces a funding round of at least $30 billion within 3 months. Probability 55 percent. Horizon: 1 to 3 months. Confidence: low. Signal: Bloomberg reports talks with United Arab Emirates funds and BlackRock, and says details could change (item 5). Confirms: a named list of investors. Weakens: a lower amount or a reported collapse of talks. Affects: OpenAI's staff and customers, then its rivals.

A. Highest conviction developments to watch. 1. Whether the Pentagon and Anthropic settle or a court rules on the supply-chain-risk label. Why: it tests whether a government can cut off a major AI supplier over its safety limits (item 1). 2. Whether Australia turns the labs' words into a breach-reporting rule. Why: it would be an early test of who must report harm caused by AI agents (item 110). 3. Whether the US 10-year yield stays above 5%. Why: the AI rally has so far held up despite it (item 8). 4. Whether the Alphabet and Constellation nuclear deal is announced, and how much power it covers. Why: electricity is the scarce input for AI data centres (item 50).

B. Low probability, high impact scenarios. 1. An AI-assisted attack on a bank or health system that forces governments to act at once, building on South Korea's warning (item 36). Probability: under 10 percent in 3 months. 2. A sharp fall in AI-linked shares as bond yields stay high, which the World Bank's warning about East Asia's dependence on AI exports makes more damaging for the region (item 18). Probability: about 10 percent in 3 months. 3. A court or regulator finds that an AI pricing system illegally coordinated prices, which the McDonald's case could test (item 111). Probability: under 10 percent in 3 months.

C. Signals that would change this view. A court order or settlement in the Anthropic dispute would weaken forecast 1. A statement from TSMC denying a January price rise would weaken forecast 4. A fall in the 10-year yield below 5% would ease the market risk (item 8). A disclosure of which AI tools were used in the South Korean bank hacks would show whether the threat is new or old methods with a new label (item 36).

D. Key unknowns and data gaps. Unknown: which AI tools were used in the South Korean bank hacks, and how large the breaches are (item 36). Unknown: whether OpenAI's Navier-Stokes claim survives expert checking (item 94). Unknown: how much nuclear power Alphabet is buying from Constellation, and where (item 50). Missing data: no confirmation from TSMC of its reported price plans (item 51). Missing data: Reuters could not verify the report that DeepSeek is close to raising about $12 billion (item 6), and the OpenAI round comes from unnamed sources (item 5). Missing data: the Pentagon's statement and reports that Claude was still used last week point in different directions (item 1).
